spatial_claims.claim: AB is a straight line with C dividing it in extreme and mean ratio; AC is the greater segment, CB the lesser; D bisects AC. Linear order: A-D-C-B.
D is the midpoint of AC, so AC = 2*DC.
DB = DC + CB, since D lies on AC between A and C, and B is beyond C (betweenness: D-C-B).
Proposition 2.4 applied to DB as the sum DC + CB: DB squared = DC squared + CB squared + 2*DC*CB.
AC decomposed as DC + DC (two equal halves); Proposition 2.4 applied: AC squared = 4*DC squared.

configuration_map: All points lie on a single straight line AB in the order A-D-C-B. D is the midpoint of AC (so AD = DC). C is the golden ratio division point with AC as the greater segment and CB as the lesser. The segment DB = DC + CB since C lies between D and B. The entire proof operates on this collinear arrangement, using algebraic identities (Propositions 2.3, 2.4, 6.17) about squares and rectangles of these segments. No angles, triangles, circles, or non-collinear points are involved.
pass_reason: All spatial claims concern collinear point ordering on a single line (A-D-C-B) and segment decompositions consistent with that ordering. The betweenness relations (D between A and C; C between D and B) are mutually consistent. The remainder of the proof is purely algebraic manipulation of segment squares and rectangles, with no angle decompositions, interior/exterior claims, or other spatial constructions that could introduce configuration contradictions.
